title: Ray Nance at the Garrick Lounge and Randolph Street clubs
summary: Correcting the earlier tape: Ray Nance played the Garrick in the 1940s during a layoff from Duke, and Roy Eldridge played across the street.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When we were talking about -- we played back reel two, and you were talking about the Garrick Lounge in Chicago.
You mentioned that on the tape you hadn't said that Ray Nance played there, or you weren't sure, but since then you had thought about it and you said Ray did play the Garrick, is that right?
And with that group he had with the three violinists in front?
No, no, no. No, no. This was much later.
Let me put it in a time context. Ray, he was -- maybe like a layoff. Duke was -- the band was kind of quiet at that point, and Ray just came home, you know?

He just came home and there he was, and he was available to play up to a certain point, when the band went on the road, when Duke went back out on the road. The six pieces, that goes way back into his young years.
I see. Yeah. I've got it right now.
You also mentioned when we were playing back that reel two something about Roy Eldridge playing -- Where?

Yeah. He was across the street from the Garrick Lounge, and I forget the name of the club. This was on Randolph Street. Randolph Street was like a short Broadway, if I can say it that way, you know. If anybody's ever been to Chicago and you see the way the 61 runs around the Loop, it -- oh, it went from State Street, maybe, over to -- about three or four blocks or something. Nothing but lights.
